title: Annotation Oracles — Mini Lab Report
content:
Purpose: quick lab notes for borderline address and phone labeling heuristics (micro-eval). Not final — messy brain dump, examples, and micro-protocol for rapid adjudication rounds.

Context and motivation:
- We've been seeing inconsistent labels for short addresses and multi-line fields where street, unit, and PO boxes mix.
- Phone normalization frequently loses extension info or confuses country codes with leading zeros.
- Need a small, high-signal sampling + adjudication protocol to stabilize rules before automating edits.

Micro-experiment setup:
- Sample 200 rows stratified by field length, presence of punctuation, and original confidence < 0.6.
- Two annotators per sample, third adjudicator for conflicts. Skip exact-match dedupe for this run.
- Capture freeform rationale (one-liner) for each conflict.

Immediate heuristics to test (fast wins):
1) Unit token heuristics: treat tokens starting with #, Apt, Unit, Ste, Suite, Bldg as unit indicators if adjacent to numeric token. If unit token appears at end, mark as UNIT and link to STREET.
2) PO/PM boxes: prefer PO_BOX label when string contains 'PO Box' or 'P.O.' (case-insensitive), even if numeric-only follows.
3) Street-number ambiguity: if first token is all digits and second token is alpha with typical street types (St, Ave, Blvd) -> STREET_NUMBER + STREET_NAME. If first token includes dash (e.g., 12-14) keep as STREET_NUMBER_RANGE.
4) Phone ext parsing: accept keywords 'ext', 'x', 'extension' followed by 1-6 digits. Keep ext as separate sublabel 'EXT'.
5) International vs local: if numeric starts with + followed by country digits -> COUNTRY_CODE. If leading 0 and length > 9, treat as local trunk prefix only if context country absent.

Representative examples and decisions (annotator expected label):
- ID 001 | raw: '123 Main St Apt 4B' | expected: 'STREET: 123 Main St' and 'UNIT: Apt 4B' | rationale: unit token at end, alpha-numeric unit -> split.
- ID 042 | raw: 'PO Box 882' | expected: 'PO_BOX: PO Box 882' | rationale: explicit PO token.
- ID 073 | raw: '12-14 W 45th St' | expected: 'STREET_NUMBER_RANGE: 12-14' and 'STREET_NAME: W 45th St' | rationale: hyphen range preserved.
- ID 128 | raw: '0044 20 7946 0958' | expected: 'PHONE: +44 20 7946 0958' with note 'leading zeros ambiguous, try to infer +44 if country context is UK in metadata' | rationale: prefer to preserve digits and surface as possible international.
- ID 158 | raw: '(415)555-0199 x231' | expected: 'PHONE: (415)555-0199' and 'EXT: 231' | rationale: standard ext marker.

Adjudication quick-protocol (for 3-person conflict resolution):
- If two annotators agree, winner. If all three different, adjudicator documents one-line rule tie-breaker and tags example for rule exception set.
- Keep a short 'why' field: one line, e.g., 'prefer PO over numeric-only' or 'treat leading + as country code'.
- Log edge samples to central sheet for weekly rule review. Link regex prototypes to Git PR.

Regex prototypes to try (fast iterations):
- unit detection: '\b(?:#|apt|unit|suite|ste|bldg)\b\s*[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,10}' (case-insensitive)
- PO box: '\bP\.??\s*O\.??\s*Box\b\s*\d+'
- ext capture: '\b(?:ext|x|extension)\b\s*[:\-]?\s*(\d{1,6})'
- phone intl heuristic: '^\+?\d[\d\s\-()]{6,}$' (then post-process to identify country code)

Open questions / edge debates to resolve in rule meeting:
- When a single token numeric looks like '10001' is it ZIP or house number? Suggest context window: if token preceded by city name -> ZIP, else if at start of string -> HOUSE_NUMBER. But many forms are incomplete.
- Multi-line fields: if second line is 1-2 tokens 'Apt 2' should always be UNIT; but some vendor feeds put apartment on same line after comma. Comma rules may break.
- International formatting: do we attempt to normalize to E164 during labeling or only tag substrings? Current vote: label raw and separate normalization pipeline.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Run first 200-sample micro-eval by 2024-11-15. (Assigned: Nate)
- Add automated script to extract conflict examples to spreadsheet and create PR with initial regex set. (Assigned: Priya)
- Draft short guideline doc with 10 canonical examples and counterexamples for new hires. (Assigned: Marco)
- Create small unit tests for regexes and attach to github PR 56.

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep rules conservative: prefer tagging not destructive normalization.
- Keep exception bucket small and explicitly list samples; these feed model-based postprocessing later.
- Capture at least one adjudication rationale per conflict.

Quick links referenced during session:
- Slack thread: #data-curation (search 'po box vs house')
- JIRA-2048: address harmonization epic
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/label-scripts/pull/56

End of dump. Will clean before formal guideline publish.
